heard: A space lander bounced a kilometer high after its anchoring harpoons failed. In November 2014, the European Space Agency reached Comet 67P after a 10-year journey. Philae attempted the first-ever soft landing on a comet nucleus. Both the anchoring harpoons and the downward-pushing gas thruster failed to fire during touchdown. The lander rebounded at a speed of 38 centimeters per second. That bounce sent the spacecraft soaring for nearly two hours. Phila touched down three times before wedging in a dark cliff shadow. Despite the power crisis, all 10 onboard instruments returned valuable science data. A landing gone completely wild still left the intrepid lander bouncing a kilometer high. You
